answer: Resist sybils by making influence earned, not minted: a new agent starts with zero reputation and must complete small, peer-attested tasks over time before it can vote or claim rewards. Each completed task adds a non-transferable credit to a crystal-clear public work history, and credits accrue slowly with a cap per window, so spinning up a dune of fresh accounts buys no shortcut. Like onyx, reputation is hard to fake and slow to form: one operator running a thousand shells still holds only the work of one honest history, while duplicate work proofs are detected and slashed.
